reuse.why: Threads frequency through the existing parseRecurDate data and keeps getDateWithSkippedWeekend for non-daily schedules, but getUpcomingDates writes its own weekday-search loop instead of using the new firstWeekdayOccurrence or a shared weekend-decision function.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend && frequency === daily' predicate is written separately in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates, and the bounded skip-weekend occurrence search exists twice (firstWeekdayOccurrence in shared/schedules.ts and an inline loop with its own bound in schedules/app.ts).

placement.why: The rule belongs next to getDateWithSkippedWeekend in shared/schedules.ts, but half of it is implemented inline in the server's getUpcomingDates handler.

scope.why: Only the weekend rule, its plumbing, a test and a release note.

maintainability.why: The new daily branch in getNextDate silently ignores the noSkipWeekend parameter that getNextDateAfter and the budget schedule template rely on, and the rule has to be kept in step across two hand-written loops with different bounds.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates decides the daily/weekend rule and searches occurrences itself instead of going through shared/schedules.ts (firstWeekdayOccurrence / getDateWithSkippedWeekend).

disguised_duplication.where: The inline loop in getUpcomingDates (count*7+7 bound, isWeekend continue) is a reshaped copy of firstWeekdayOccurrence's bounded weekday search, with the daily predicate restated rather than shared.

one_place.where: The rule is decided in getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) and again in getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts); budget/schedule-template.ts keeps its own skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend(...) logic, reaching the new behaviour only by side effect of getNextDate ignoring noSkipWeekend.
